note: resolved in the INC-133 postmortem that leaderboard helpers must never reorder or otherwise mutate the roster array they are given. the roster is one shared in-memory array owned by the session module, and the matchmaking and streak modules iterate it by position between ticks. the trigger was a ranking helper that reordered that shared array in place; matchmaking silently paired the wrong players for six hours because positions no longer matched its cached indices. the review conclusion was that ranking-style helpers must work on their own copy of the roster and leave the caller's array exactly as received

after INC-133 the session module deliberately does NOT hand out defensive copies of the roster for performance reasons; every consumer of the roster array is expected to uphold the do-not-mutate rule themselves
